steps.premise: Stacks can hide the range of postcard pictures.
steps.action: Stand one card from each design upright.
steps.consequence: Visitors can see and choose a familiar view.
steps.quote: A row of card stacks hides most of the pictures. Prop up one of each design so visitors can pick out a view they recognize.

steps.premise: A writer gets stuck just after the greeting.
steps.action: Ask about something they saw on the way to the table.
steps.consequence: The question gives them a concrete detail to include.
steps.quote: Someone who stalls after “Dear Nan” might welcome a question like “What did you see on the way here?” It gives them a detail to write about.

steps.premise: The required postage depends on the destination.
steps.action: Ask where the card will go before giving out a stamp.
steps.consequence: A card going abroad receives the proper postage.
steps.quote: Postage depends on where the card is going, so have the stamp volunteer ask the destination before handing over a stamp. That keeps a card for overseas from leaving with domestic postage.

steps.premise: The writer might use the address area for their message.
steps.action: Show an example address on a large demonstration card.
steps.consequence: The writer can leave the correct half free.
steps.quote: Put a sample address on an oversized card. People can see which half they need to leave free before their message fills it.

steps.premise: A visitor in a wheelchair wants to write with friends.
steps.action: Keep a place open at the end of the table.
steps.consequence: They can pull up and write beside the others.
steps.quote: An empty space at the end of the table lets someone pull up in a wheelchair and write alongside their friends.

steps.premise: A child has a story but cannot yet write the letters.
steps.action: Have a volunteer write down what the child dictates.
steps.consequence: The card carries the child's own words.
steps.quote: A child may have a whole story to send before they can form the letters. A volunteer who takes dictation can get the child's own words onto the card.

steps.premise: A visitor must check part of the address at home.
steps.action: Give them a protective sleeve for the unfinished card.
steps.consequence: It can go in their bag without bending.
steps.quote: If a visitor needs to look up a house number at home, give them a sleeve for the unfinished card. It can travel in their bag without getting bent.

steps.premise: Some visitors will come later in the day.
steps.action: Set aside several designs for the afternoon.
steps.consequence: Latecomers still get a choice of pictures.
steps.quote: Keep a few card designs in reserve for the afternoon so late arrivals still have a choice of pictures.

steps.premise: A writer wants to record where and when the visit happened.
steps.action: Display the town and current date at the writing spots.
steps.consequence: Visitors can copy the details without breaking off a conversation.
steps.quote: Print the town and today's date on a small sign at the writing places. Visitors who want to mark the occasion can copy both without interrupting a conversation.

steps.premise: Completed cards are waiting for pickup.
steps.action: Collect them face down in a shallow slotted box.
steps.consequence: Other people cannot see them as they wait.
steps.quote: A shallow box with a slot keeps completed cards face down and out of view while they wait for collection.

steps.premise: Selecting a picture can take time for a family.
steps.action: Place the card selection a short distance away from the writing seats.
steps.consequence: Someone can write while the family chooses a design.
steps.quote: One person can write while a family debates which picture to send if the card display sits a few steps away from the writing seats.

steps.premise: Printed colors can look different from the original scene.
steps.action: Identify the photographer's location on the reverse of each card.
steps.consequence: The recipient can recognize where the view was taken.
steps.quote: A blue sky can look quite different once a card is printed. Put the photographer's location on the back so recipients can still identify the view.

steps.premise: Visitors between buses have limited time.
steps.action: Display the final collection time.
steps.consequence: They can choose whether to leave the card or mail it themselves.
steps.quote: Some visitors will arrive between buses. Posting the last collection time lets them decide whether to leave the card with the volunteers or post it themselves.

steps.premise: Wind can scatter loose postcards outdoors.
steps.action: Secure the stock under a wide paperweight.
steps.consequence: Visitors can take one card at a time while the rest stay put.
steps.quote: A gust can carry half a dozen postcards across the square. Tuck the outdoor stock under a broad paperweight so people can lift out one card at a time.

steps.premise: A spoken invitation may miss people who use other languages.
steps.action: Display a welcome sign in the languages local people commonly read.
steps.consequence: Visitors can recognize that they are invited to participate.
steps.quote: Visitors who use different languages may miss a spoken invitation. A welcome sign in the languages commonly read in town helps them see they can join in.

steps.premise: A pen may skip on the glossy postcard surface.
steps.action: Try the pens on a real card before opening.
steps.consequence: Volunteers can replace a poor pen before it damages a message.
steps.quote: Test the pens on an actual postcard before opening. A pen that skips on the glossy stock can be replaced before it spoils someone's message.

steps.premise: Thin pens can tire a writer with stiff fingers.
steps.action: Fit some pens with a broad grip.
steps.consequence: The writer can finish a longer message comfortably.
steps.quote: A writer with stiff fingers may find a narrow pen tiring. Slip a wide grip onto a few pens so a longer message is comfortable to finish.

steps.premise: Visitors need to know the cost before taking a seat.
steps.action: Label the cost of both the card and stamp by the entrance, including free items.
steps.consequence: People know what they can take before they sit.
steps.quote: Mark the price of a card and stamp at the entrance, including either one that's free, so visitors know what they can take before they sit down.

steps.premise: Lines can drift together on the blank side of a card.
steps.action: Use a short ruler as a guide and move it down while writing.
steps.consequence: The lines stay apart.
steps.quote: A short ruler makes a good line guide on the blank side. Writers can move it down as they go and keep their lines from drifting into each other.

steps.premise: Visitors may finish cards just before closing.
steps.action: Assign a volunteer to bring the collection box to the post office at closing.
steps.consequence: Someone is responsible for mailing even the last cards.
steps.quote: Name a volunteer to take the collection box to the post office at closing. Cards left in the final few minutes then have someone responsible for getting them into the mail.
